title: Recursive Zig-Zag SPRP Security Beyond the Hidden-Set Model
summary: Under the material baseline condition, the analysis covers a uniformly hidden preserved-set model; extending SPRP security to other distributions or adversary-knowledge models remains open.

formal_statement.body: For $t \le d-n$, extend the SPRP-security analysis of Recursive Zig-Zag domain extension beyond the model in which $T$ is chosen uniformly from the size-$t$ subsets of the original domain $D$ and is hidden from the adversary, to other adversarial distributions over $T$ or other adversary-knowledge models for $T$.

scope.domain: SPRP security analysis for Recursive Zig-Zag domain extension in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: the adversary knows the original domain D
the preserved set T is chosen uniformly from the size-t subsets of D and is hidden from the adversary
parameters: t: size of the preserved set
d and n: parameters in the baseline condition
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the SPRP-security analysis to other adversarial distributions over T or other adversary-knowledge models for T.

citations.label: Modifying an Enciphering Scheme After Deployment

progress.summary: The source presents SPRP security when T is chosen uniformly from size-t subsets of D and hidden from the adversary, then explicitly says that treating other cases is an open question.
citation_labels: Paul Grubbs et al., Modifying an Enciphering Scheme After Deployment
